label: May 1915
headline: The Shell Scandal
deck: Attacks in Artois fail for want of guns and shells; London is shaken
caption: Gunners stack a thin row of shells beside a field gun near Festubert
body: On 9 May the French Tenth Army attacks in Artois after a long bombardment. In the centre the Moroccan Division storms forward some three miles in ninety minutes and reaches the crest of Vimy Ridge, but the reserves are too far back, and German counter-attacks drive it off again.

On the same morning, a few miles to the north, the British attack Aubers Ridge. Their short bombardment barely touches the German wire and breastworks, and the attack is stopped within hours at heavy cost. At Festubert, a week later, they win little more.

On 14 May The Times reports that a lack of high-explosive shells cost the British their success. The storm in Parliament and the press is joined by another: Admiral Fisher resigns as First Sea Lord over the Dardanelles, Churchill leaves the Admiralty, and Lloyd George is named to a new Ministry of Munitions.
briefs: A troop train is wrecked near Gretna; over 200 Scottish soldiers die
A Zeppelin bombs London for the first time, on 31 May
The Allies warn the Ottoman government over massacres of Armenians
